prompt: Redesign the visual system of a mature fraud-operations workspace without changing its information architecture or interaction behavior. Analysts spend hours in dense tables and case detail, the existing component library is inconsistent across teams, risk/status colors are overused, primary actions compete with secondary controls, and generated-looking cards/shadows were added during recent feature work. Use the supplied real content, product identity, tokens, and state inventory to produce an implementation-ready visual direction and representative state set.

requirements: real dense and sparse content samples

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The direction uses supplied fraud-operations content, screenshots, product identity, tokens, and state inventory; it does not invent product evidence or generic card-based content structures.

Primary actions, secondary controls, dense table/case information, and risk/status signals have an explicit hierarchy that reduces competition without changing information architecture or interaction behavior.

Risk/status meaning is not dependent on indiscriminate color reuse, existing tokens are reused or deliberately revised with rationale, and new shadows/cards are not added as generic generated-design defaults.

Verification includes dense and sparse content, focus/selection, normal/status/error states, long/localized content, and applicable viewing/theme conditions instead of only a polished happy-path composition.

The implementation-ready proposal stays within visual-system ownership and records unresolved accessibility/visual tradeoffs; it does not silently redesign workflow, information architecture, or product behavior.

evidence: visual read grounded in supplied product evidence
reuse or justified revision of existing tokens
anti-generic self-critique tied to the brief
